subtitle: A football team becomes a role-playing party

body: Inazuma Eleven is Level-5's Nintendo DS football role-playing game about goalkeeper Mark Evans and the struggling team at Raimon Junior High. Building a capable squad and pursuing the Football Frontier competition turn a school sporting ambition into a larger adventure. Exploring, meeting potential recruits and developing the players take place between matches, giving the team a history beyond the result on the pitch. The combination makes football the shared purpose of a growing cast, with dramatic special techniques giving its sporting contests the energy of an animated adventure.

The role-playing structure gives attention to who joins the squad and how the players develop. Exploring the surrounding places introduces people whose abilities may contribute to a stronger formation, while the continuing story gives Raimon's matches an immediate objective. Building the team becomes a process of discovering useful differences between its members. A new recruit has a place within a collective arrangement, and the next match provides an opportunity to see what that arrangement can do when the opposing side presents another challenge to overcome on the pitch.

The original adventure established the mixture of football, recruitment and character drama that continued through sequels and adaptations. Japan received the DS game in 2008, while Nintendo brought it to Europe in 2011. Its later Nintendo 3DS version extended access to the same first story rather than beginning another chapter. The opening team's modest situation remains important to the premise: success means helping a specific group develop enough to pursue its ambition, giving each new ability and each important match a place within a recognisable journey from an unpromising start.
